The operating range for BESS.V∗ and i BESS.f∗ is based on common practice, which can differ across manufacturers. BESS.P∗ is the active i i power command/set point for the i−th BESS when the operating mode BESS.Mode=GFL. When the i operating mode of the i−th BESS is GFM, the voltage set point and frequency set point are denoted as BESS.V∗ and BESS.f∗, respectively, and they are specified as a percentage of the nominal voltage i i (V :=480 V) and frequency (f :=60 Hz). The idle mode represents a state where the BESS unit nominal nominal is ready to operate in either GFM or GFL mode and is awaiting a command from the PFMS. The BESS unit could be available if it has sufficient stored energy, or it could be unavailable for use if the SOC is too low or due to any other internal fault condition of the unit. The availability aspect of the unit is defined by BESS.Available field. The BESS units are modeled using a DRTS library model. i Although any type or count of backup power units can be added to the Verrus medium-voltage power do- main (up to the rating threshold of the medium-voltage power infrastructure), for demonstration purposes, the representation in the Vulcan model is a full complement of standby diesel generators (70 MVA). The diesel generator units, rated at 3.5 MVA each (Plimit), connect to the medium-voltage power distribution gen through breakers X ,X ,...,X . The aggregate generator capacity is 77 MW, and it has the redundant g,1 g,2 g,n generator unit capacity baked in. The diesel generator units are used only during grid outages after the energy stored in the BESS has depleted to a minimum threshold; thus, the generator capacity is sized to support the entire 70 MW of the data center IT and cooling loads.
